title: A2 review: a whole trip
topic: big review of the A2 level
why: This big review covers the whole A2 level through a complete trip around Andalusia: the three past tenses for telling stories, travel phrases and complaints, pronouns, comparatives, the future, the conditional and the imperative. It closes A2 and takes stock of what the learner has mastered before moving on to B1.

{"lessons": ["

Telling the story of the trip: three past tenses

To tell the story of a trip, you have three past tenses, and each one has its job:

TenseJobExample
perfectopast linked to today (hoy, esta semana, ya, todavía no), like English \"I have done\"Esta mañana he vuelto de Andalucía.
indefinidofinished action, at a finished time (ayer, el lunes, la semana pasada), like English \"I did\"El lunes fuimos a Córdoba.
imperfectobackground, description, habit (hacía, era, había), like \"it was…\" or \"I used to…\"Hacía calor y las calles estaban llenas de flores.
estar in the imperfect + gerundaction in progress, interrupted (\"I was doing\")Estábamos cenando cuando empezó el flamenco.

Here's a short story that mixes all three:

Esta semana he estado en Sevilla. El primer día fuimos a la catedral. Hacía muchísimo calor, pero en los patios había sombra y flores por todas partes. Por la noche, mientras cenábamos, un grupo empezó a tocar flamenco.This week I've been in Seville. On the first day, we went to the cathedral. It was incredibly hot, but in the patios there was shade and there were flowers everywhere. In the evening, while we were having dinner, a group started playing flamenco.

Reminder: in Spain, hoy and esta semana call for the perfecto, even where English might say \"I went this morning\"; ayer and el año pasado call for the indefinido. The imperfect sets the scene: \"it was hot,\" \"it was,\" \"there were.\"

To link the steps: primero, luego, después, de repente, al día siguiente, al final. And to react to a friend's story: ¡No me digas!, ¿Y qué pasó?, ¡Qué envidia!

", "

During the trip: everything you can say

SituationSentenceTranslation
at the stationUn billete de ida y vuelta para Sevilla, por favor.A round-trip ticket to Seville, please.
¿A qué hora sale el próximo AVE?What time does the next AVE leave?
at the hotelTengo una reserva a nombre de Martín.I have a reservation under the name Martín.
a problemEl aire acondicionado no funciona. ¿Podría cambiarme la habitación?The air conditioning doesn't work. Could you give me a different room?
at the restaurant¿Qué me recomienda?What do you recommend?
directionsPerdone, ¿para ir a la catedral? —Siga todo recto y gire a la derecha.Excuse me, how do I get to the cathedral? — Go straight ahead and turn right.
in a store¿Puedo probármelo? Me queda un poco grande.Can I try it on? It's a little big on me.
comparingCórdoba es más tranquila que Sevilla.Córdoba is quieter than Seville.

Pronouns, everywhere

As soon as you've already named something, replace it: ¿Las entradas? Ya las he comprado. / ¿La llave? Se la he dado a la recepcionista. / ¿Me lo puede envolver? Es un regalo.

With usted (hotel, station, restaurant), the verb is in the 3rd person, the imperative takes its special form (siga, gire, perdone) and the indirect pronoun is le: ¿Le puedo hacer una pregunta?

", "

What's next? Plans, advice, invitations

To express…SentenceTranslation
a decided planEste verano voy a volver a Cádiz.This summer, I'm going to go back to Cádiz.
a distant plan, a promiseAlgún día viviré en Granada.Someday, I'll live in Granada.
a guessAhora habrá menos turistas.There must be fewer tourists right now.
a wishMe encantaría ver la Feria de Sevilla.I'd love to see the Seville Fair.
adviceYo que tú, iría en primavera.If I were you, I'd go in the spring.
an invitation¿Te apetece venir conmigo?Do you feel like coming with me?

Your A2 review

Congratulations: with this lesson, you've completed the A2 level. You can now:

  • tell stories in the past, choosing between perfecto, indefinido and imperfecto;
  • get by while traveling: tickets, hotel, restaurant, directions, complaints;
  • give instructions in the imperative, with tú and with usted;
  • replace nouns with pronouns, even double ones (se lo, dámelo);
  • talk about the future, be polite, give advice and invite people;
  • compare things and go shopping.

Next step, B1: the working world, relative pronouns, por and para, and a big newcomer, the subjunctive.
